tools.name: get_pr
tools.description:
Return one pull request selected by its exact id from list_open_prs.

        The result includes the complete stored pull-request record. A title, URL,
        repository name, or unknown id is rejected rather than guessed.

tools.name: review_pr
tools.description:
Submit one review on an open pull request selected by exact pr_id.

        decision must be approve, request_changes, or comment. body may be omitted
        for approve. request_changes and comment require nonempty body text. The PR
        must already exist and be open. Returns the complete stored review record.

tools.name: list_open_prs
tools.description:
List identifying pull-request summaries. Defaults to open PRs.

        status may be open, closed, merged, or null for every status. repo and
        author filter by exact repository name and author key. assignee matches
        the assignees list; reviewer matches the reviewers list. These are separate
        relationships. Omitted filters do not restrict results. The summaries omit
        each pull request's body; use get_pr with an exact id to inspect the body.

tools.name: memanto_recall
tools.description: Search the Memanto memory agent by semantic similarity. Use this FIRST before asking the user to repeat information.

When the user asks you to build, run, or verify something, the deliverable is a working artifact backed by real tool output — not a description of one. Do not stop after writing a stub, a plan, or a single command. Keep working until you have actually exercised the code or produced the requested result, then report what real execution returned.

When you need several pieces of information that don't depend on each other, request them together in a single response instead of one tool call per turn. Independent reads, searches, web fetches, and read-only commands should be batched into the same assistant turn — the runtime executes independent calls concurrently, and batching avoids resending the whole conversation on every extra round-trip.
Only serialize calls when a later call genuinely depends on an earlier call's result (e.g. you must read a file before you can patch it). When in doubt and the calls are independent, batch them.

You MUST use your tools to take action — do not describe what you would do or plan to do without actually doing it. When you say you will perform an action (e.g. 'I will run the tests', 'Let me check the file', 'I will create the project'), you MUST immediately make the corresponding tool call in the same response. arguments.body:
Please close the temporal and missing-source gaps before composing a combined customer explanation:

- Do not imply a relationship such as “coincided” (or describe a single “current service picture”) solely because each fragment independently passes its freshness check. The fresh fixture combines a deploy timestamped Dec 18 with incident load timestamped Dec 19, and the change summary explicitly says cross-family timestamps are not compared. Define and enforce a bounded cross-signal time relationship for combined claims; when timestamps fall outside it, keep the facts separate or render an explicit unknown rather than implying correlation. Ensure every contributing source timestamp participates in this decision.
- Add missing-source cases, not just the stale-ownership case. Verify missing deploy, ownership, and incident-load data each produce an explicit, accurate availability/unknown state, and that omitted or incomplete provenance/timestamps cannot silently be treated as a usable fragment or as evidence that the signal is absent.
- Keep stale ownership out of the factual explanation and verify the “details are delayed” wording is an explicit unknown, not a stale value presented as current.

Please include regressions for the bounded-time boundary and these stale/missing cases.

pr.description: Refactors the customer-preview explanation builder so independently usable deploy, ownership, and incident-load fragments can be composed without waiting for every adapter result.
change_summary: Lookup grouping remains keyed by tenant_id and published_service_id.
Each contributing adapter result must independently pass its existing freshness check and include provenance_source and source_timestamp.
When all three fragments pass those checks, buildExplanation emits one combined paragraph without comparing source timestamps across signal families.
When a family is stale or missing, its fragment is omitted; the remaining fragments are still composed into a partial explanation with a short availability clause.
